records.c: object type 15, the level's end boss: a machine of five columns and seven rows of sprites ($BE to $FA), drawn by sprites 3 to 7 used again for each row by interrupts of its own, all in one colour ($7975). It comes in from past the right edge and creeps left a pixel every sixth frame, 238 pixels in all, while the claws at its front snap open and shut. Only shots at the middle of its front take energy; it has 2,801. Destroyed, it flickers, flies apart into eleven pieces and gives 10,000 points
its first frame waits, the object left new, until the hero is on the ground ($29, $26 zero) and the fine scroll is at rest ($17 = 4, $16 = 3)

takes the screen over: its own sprites ($03ED), the scroll stopped ($084D to the RTS at $085D, $0718 and $071A to the interrupt's exit), its raster routine $765B in place of the multiplexer ($071E), and $75C4 and $72CF in the level's frame vectors ($0862, $0865). 238 steps of creeping, one every 6 frames ($BE30, $BE31), 2,801 energy ($BE32, $BE33), the claws' timer and step ($BE37, $BE38); every other object is removed, and the object loop ends with it this frame ($0859 = 0)
the rows' Y: row 0's from $7924 by the view's row ($0B less $43: 65, 57 or 49), the others 21 lines apart
writes the shown screen's page plus 3 ($0205) into the five STAs of the raster routine that set the sprite pointers

the machine's routine each frame after the first: puts back the top lines lent at the last row ($77D7); while it lives, white again ($7975), tests for shots ($73EF) and touching the hero ($748F). While the hero is in the air his three sprites are placed at once ($D000-$D004). Then the creeping ($733D), the claws ($7523), and the first row for the next frame ($72CF)
the machine's slot back in X; while it lives (state 0), white again and the tests for shots and for touching the hero

finds the first row whose Y is on the play area ($34 to $D5); a row above it that reaches into the top of the screen is shown first ($0224), with the first interrupt a line above the next row ($03EB). When that line is a bad one the next row's top lines are lent ($772D)
the top row is on the screen: sprites 3 to 7 take its Y at once

destroyed, it goes to $73A4. Otherwise, while steps are left ($BE30), every sixth frame all five columns move a pixel left, each borrow flipping that column's high bit ($793F); then rows 1 to 6 take row 0's X and high bits. At the start all five high bits are set, so the machine begins at X 344, past the right edge
the machine is destroyed: its colour flips between white and black each frame for 51 frames ($BE34)

gives the screen back to the engine: its sprites, the multiplexer ($071E from $0872) and the scroll ($084D from $0876); all eleven object slots become its debris (type 14, new), two sounds ($89, $8A) and 10,000 points ($0211 = 1)

looks for the hero's shots down 14 character rows from 16 lines below row 0's Y, each row two characters wide at a column from $7927, measured from column 0's left edge. A shot found becomes $D4 (a grenade told it hit, a laser stopped); only rows 6 to 8 of the 14, the middle of the front, take energy
a hit in the middle: black for a frame ($7975), and the weapon's damage from $0720 comes off the energy ($BE32, $BE33). Below zero it is destroyed (state 1, 51 frames); otherwise the sound $8B

object type 3, the sliding block (sprite $98, white): sits still until shot, then slides 3 units a frame away from the hero, turning round at walls with the sound $A3, until it leaves the screen. Nothing destroys it, and touching it hurts the hero unless he is shielded or the wheel

object type 4, the spike ball: a big one (sprites $99-$9C, turning as it rolls) rolls a unit a frame towards where the hero was when it came, bouncing off floors in high arcs and off walls the other way, with the sound $8B. Shot, it bursts with 400 points into two small balls ($9D) that bounce off at random; each small one shot is an explosion and 400 points more. Touching either hurts the hero, unless he is shielded or the wheel, which destroys it for the same points
